deviations.what: The object-typed calendar date properties (Calendar.minDate, Calendar.maxDate and the disabledDates DateRange startDate/endDate) are fed from plain ISO strings in the model and converted at the point of use with Formatter.DateCreateObject from the curated module (core:require='{Formatter: z2ui5/model/formatter}'). A plain string binding would crash view creation (Date must be a JS/UI5Date object). The original's UI5Date.getInstance(year, month0, day) values are normalized to ISO 1:1 (month is 0-based: minDate 2000-01-01, maxDate 2050-12-31, disabled ranges 2016-01-04..2016-01-10 and 2016-01-15). The second disabled range omits endDate in the original (a single day); it serializes here as an empty end field.

Review finding 2026-07-27, open: the empty end field of the second disabled range is a crash risk, not just a caveat. Formatter.DateCreateObject('') returns new Date('') = Invalid Date, DateRange.endDate accepts it (type object), and sap.ui.unified Month._checkDateEnabled runs CalendarDate.fromLocalJSDate on every truthy endDate, which throws 'Date parameter must be a JavaScript or UI5Date date object' on Invalid Date (source-verified in Month.js/CalendarDate.js; MonthRenderer calls _checkDateEnabled per rendered day). The original avoids this because its JS row simply omits end (undefined is falsy). Needs rework - e.g. split the bound disabledDates aggregation into per-shape entries so the single-day row carries no endDate binding - before this port can be promoted. render-smoke cannot see it (mocked model).

The Calendar select handler (handleCalendarSelect) formats the picked day with DateFormat and writes it into the 'selectedDate' Text; this is imperative presentation with no bindable equivalent (the select event parameter is a DateRange control reference, not a value that can be transported), so the select attribute is dropped and the selectedDate Text keeps its initial 'No Date Selected' text.

The original Switch (state='true') toggles Calendar week numbers via an imperative change handler (setShowWeekNumbers). This is folded into a two-way binding shared by the Switch state and a Calendar showWeekNumbers property (both bound to show_week_numbers, seeded true), so the toggle runs on the client with no round-trip - the thin-frontend move. The Switch change attribute is therefore dropped and a showWeekNumbers attribute (absent from the original view) is added.

Formatter.DateCreateObject is referenced via core:require, which needs UI5 >= 1.74. sap.ui.unified.Calendar itself and its minDate/maxDate/disabledDates/showWeekNumbers members are all <= 1.71 (in scope).
